Pod.title: Pod
Pod.simple: The smallest unit Kubernetes runs: one or more containers running together on the same node, sharing network and volumes.
Pod.technical: It has a lifecycle (Pending → Running → Succeeded/Failed), its own IP, health probes and requested/limited resources. Usually created by a controller (Deployment, StatefulSet, Job) that recreates it if lost.

Deployment.title: Deployment
Deployment.simple: Manages one or more copies of your application and lets you update them progressively.
Deployment.technical: Creates a ReplicaSet for each template version; the rolling update moves replicas from the old to the new ReplicaSet respecting maxSurge/maxUnavailable and readiness probes. Keeps revisions for rollback.

ReplicaSet.title: ReplicaSet
ReplicaSet.simple: Keeps an exact number of identical Pod copies running. Usually managed by a Deployment.
ReplicaSet.technical: Each Deployment revision corresponds to a ReplicaSet with a different pod-template-hash.

StatefulSet.title: StatefulSet
StatefulSet.simple: Like a Deployment, but for applications with data (databases, queues): each copy has a stable name and its own disk.
StatefulSet.technical: Numbered Pods (name-0, name-1…), ordered start and update, volumeClaimTemplates for a dedicated PVC per replica, headless Service for stable DNS.

DaemonSet.title: DaemonSet
DaemonSet.simple: Runs one copy of a Pod on every node (or a group of nodes): typical for monitoring, log and network agents.
DaemonSet.technical: The number of Pods follows the number of eligible nodes (nodeSelector, tolerations); updates roll node by node.

Job.title: Job
Job.simple: Runs a task to completion (e.g. a migration) and then stops.
Job.technical: completions/parallelism define how many runs are needed; backoffLimit the retries; activeDeadlineSeconds the maximum time.

CronJob.title: CronJob
CronJob.simple: Creates a Job on a schedule, like Linux cron (e.g. a nightly backup).
CronJob.technical: Cron-format schedule, concurrencyPolicy (Allow/Forbid/Replace), history of successful/failed Jobs, suspend to pause it.

Service.title: Service
Service.simple: Gives a stable name and address to a group of Pods and spreads traffic across the ready copies.
Service.technical: The selector finds the Pods; only Ready ones enter the Endpoints. Types: ClusterIP (internal), NodePort (port on every node), LoadBalancer (external IP), headless (DNS of single Pods).

Ingress.title: Ingress
Ingress.simple: Makes a web application reachable from outside through a host name and path (e.g. https://shop.example.com/).
Ingress.technical: Host/path rules to Services; requires an Ingress Controller (e.g. nginx); TLS through a kubernetes.io/tls Secret.

Endpoints.title: Endpoints
Endpoints.simple: The list of addresses of the ready Pods a Service sends traffic to.
Endpoints.technical: Updated automatically by the controller based on the Service selector and Pod readiness.

PersistentVolume.title: PersistentVolume
PersistentVolume.simple: A disk made available to the cluster, which outlives Pods.
PersistentVolume.technical: Created manually or dynamically by a StorageClass; has capacity, access mode and reclaimPolicy (Delete/Retain).

PersistentVolumeClaim.title: PersistentVolumeClaim
PersistentVolumeClaim.simple: An application's request for disk space: Kubernetes binds it to a suitable volume.
PersistentVolumeClaim.technical: Specifies size, access mode and StorageClass; goes from Pending to Bound when a PV is bound.

StorageClass.title: StorageClass
StorageClass.simple: A kind of storage available in the cluster, which creates disks automatically when needed.
StorageClass.technical: Defines the provisioner, parameters, reclaimPolicy and volumeBindingMode (Immediate or WaitForFirstConsumer).

ConfigMap.title: ConfigMap
ConfigMap.simple: Non-secret configuration (files or variables) kept outside the container image.
ConfigMap.technical: Mounted as files or exposed as environment variables; mounted file changes propagate, variable changes need a restart.

Secret.title: Secret
Secret.simple: Confidential data (passwords, tokens, certificates) used by applications.
Secret.technical: Base64-encoded values (not encrypted by default in the API); access must be restricted with RBAC. In PKM values are hidden and viewing them is audited.

Node.title: Node
Node.simple: A machine (physical or virtual) of the cluster that runs Pods.
Node.technical: The kubelet reports status (Ready, memory/disk/PID pressure), capacity and allocatable resources; taints restrict which Pods can run there.

Namespace.title: Namespace
Namespace.simple: A logical folder separating applications and environments (e.g. production, staging) in the same cluster.
Namespace.technical: Scope for names, quotas, RBAC and network policies. Deleting a namespace deletes all its content.

Event.title: Event
Event.simple: A Kubernetes message about something that happened to a resource (start, error, restart…).
Event.technical: Events have a type (Normal/Warning), reason, count and expire after about one hour.

PodDisruptionBudget.title: PodDisruptionBudget
PodDisruptionBudget.simple: Guarantees that a minimum number of application copies stays up during maintenance.
PodDisruptionBudget.technical: minAvailable or maxUnavailable; honoured by the Eviction API (drain), not by failures.

HorizontalPodAutoscaler.title: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
HorizontalPodAutoscaler.simple: Automatically increases or decreases replicas based on load.
HorizontalPodAutoscaler.technical: Uses metrics (CPU, memory, custom) and scales the target between minReplicas and maxReplicas.
